decisions.text: type bar: categories compared by value
clustered bars: 4 series of one measure across categories (G1.56, R9-12)
nominal categories sorted by value, descending (by series ops)
4 series side by side in each cluster, the bars touching, in the same order in every cluster: Operations (slot 1), Finance (slot 2), Support (slot 3), Other depts (all-others) (G7.5, G4.22)
every name fits under its bar, neighbours at least 10 pt apart: vertical bars
the unit phrase on the top label: “140 employees”; the top gridline starts after it
a legend above the plot, below the title, centred over the plot: labels beside the bars of a cluster would each need a leader (G5.7, G5.10, D-7)
legend entries in the order of the bars in each cluster, left to right: Operations, Finance, Support, Other depts (G5.8, G5.14: square keys)

findings.message: the unit phrase “employees” is one word; say what is counted, which subset and per what period

source.shows: the book's good version: a legend row above the plot whose entries run in the order and direction of the bars in each cluster (G5.8, G5.10); “Other depts”, a catch-all, in its reserved grey (G4.15; the book draws it gold), and the regions sorted by the first series (D-46; the book keeps them unsorted)
